idiom_name: using / await using declarations + Disposable, AsyncDisposable and DisposableStack types
implementation_notes: TypeScript implements ECMAScript explicit resource management and types it: a using/await using declaration binds a value whose [Symbol.dispose]/[Symbol.asyncDispose] runs at scope exit, and for targets below ES2026 the compiler emits the equivalent try/finally plus a helper - so the deterministic release is produced at compile time, checked against the lib that provides Symbol.dispose and the Disposable global types. TypeScript also supplies Disposable, AsyncDisposable and the DisposableStack/AsyncDisposableStack types (5.6+) for defer-style stacks and move semantics over several resources. As in JavaScript the contract belongs to the object: an owner implements [Symbol.dispose] idempotently and cascades only to owned resources, while explicit try/finally remains the manual form for older engines or when the release has to be observed by callers.
pitfalls: using requires the disposable lib reference and downlevel emission adds helper code, so the compiled bundle - not just the source - must be verified; older targets need a Symbol.dispose polyfill.
The binding is readonly and the value must satisfy Disposable (or be null/undefined), but any structurally matching object is accepted, including one that does not own the resource.
The value can escape the scope through a closure or a returned object exactly as in JavaScript; types do not prevent returning an already-disposed resource.
